Hi Carlos. The new standard is published, and it starts in June. Did you read it?
Yes, Emma. I read the first part, but some sentences are difficult for me.
Which ones?
For example: "Records are kept for three years." Who keeps them? The sentence does not say.
That is normal in a standard. The action is important, not the person. The farms keep the records.
I understand now. And the audit? How often is a farm audited?
Every farm is audited every twelve months. The certificate is renewed after a good audit.
And the evidence?
Evidence is requested for every criterion. Please send me your evidence folder by Friday.
Of course, Emma. I am going to send it tomorrow.

When I read a certification standard, I do not look for names. I look for actions. The rules are always written in the same way. Records are kept for three years. Evidence is requested for every criterion. The farm is audited every twelve months. Nobody says who does the work, because the action is the important part. After my last visit, the report was sent to Geneva and the farm was approved. The certificate was renewed for one more year.

Hi Carlos, this is Emma. Three quick points about the new standard. First, the scope: this year only the coffee area is audited, not the whole property. Second, the evidence: every document is checked, so please keep the original papers. Third, one date: the audit is scheduled for June fifteenth, and the certificate is renewed in July. Your evidence folder was received this morning. Thank you, Carlos. Talk soon.

First, the standard: the new rules are published in June. Then the evidence: every document is requested and checked. Next, the audit: the farm is audited by an external team. After that, the result: the report was sent to Geneva and the farm was approved. Finally, the certificate: the certificate is renewed for one more year.
